title: EDA mini project, Git/Linux/HTTP refresh + PairCraft auth & sync v1
objective: Ship an honest EDA on a messy dataset; refresh Git internals, Linux shell and HTTP precisely; build PairCraft auth, rooms and editor sync v1.
topics: Cloud track: AWS core concepts + account safety
Git: rebase, cherry-pick, conflicts, clean history
Linux: processes, permissions, pipes, grep/awk/sed, ssh
HTTP precisely: methods, status codes, headers, caching, cookies
PairCraft: JWT auth, RBAC, rooms, editor sync v1
theory: What a “finding” is vs a chart; why last-write-wins is a starting point for sync, not the end.
practice: Mini project #2 EDA; Missing Semester lectures; PairCraft build.
deliverables: EDA repo with notebook + exported HTML + README findings
PairCraft: register/login/refresh, rooms with roles, shared editor with versioned ops
checkpoint: Two browsers see each other typing in PairCraft

knowledge: Rebase vs merge: when do you refuse to rebase?
Which HTTP methods are idempotent and why does it matter for retries?
Why is last-write-wins insufficient for a collaborative editor?
practical: Reproduce the EDA with one command
Solve Search in Rotated Sorted Array cold

MERN revision · Node: event loop phases, libuv, streams (readable/writable/transform, backpressure), buffers, worker threads vs cluster, process signals + graceful shutdown. Stream a 1 GB file through a transform with backpressure; add graceful shutdown to PairCraft’s server.

Cloud track: create an AWS IAM admin boundary using a non-root daily user, enable MFA, set a budget alert, then deploy a minimal EC2 or container service. Write down region/AZ, security-group and billing choices.
